issues.description: The solution repository's Person class declares the last-name field as 'surname' but all accessors and equality/hashCode methods refer to 'lastName'. The template (and intended model) uses the field name 'lastName'. This mismatch (field name/identifier inconsistency) will cause compilation errors in the solution and confuses students about the correct attribute name to use when implementing tests and service logic.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the field name consistent. Either rename the field in the solution from 'surname' back to 'lastName' (to match the template and the getters/setters), or update all getters, setters, equals, and hashCode to consistently use 'surname'. The simplest fix to preserve consistency with the template and problem description is to change 'private String surname;' to 'private String lastName;'.

issues.description: The Person entity's last-name attribute is inconsistently named across artifacts. In the template and tests the attribute is represented as 'lastName' (with corresponding getters/setters used by tests), whereas the solution's Person.java declares the field as 'surname' but its getters/setters and equals/hashCode still reference 'lastName'. This creates a broken and confusing mapping: students and tests expect 'lastName', but the solution's field name differs and the code is internally inconsistent. This discrepancy is likely unintentional and will prevent straightforward mapping between problem requirements, template code, and the solution (and may break compilation/runtime behavior).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the last-name identifier consistent across all artifacts. The simplest correction is to rename the field in the solution's Person.java from 'surname' to 'lastName' (or conversely rename all references and tests to 'surname'), and ensure getters/setters, equals(), and hashCode() consistently use the same identifier. Prefer aligning to 'lastName' to match the template and existing tests.
